drivingQuestion: In which cases is a slaughterer exempt from giving the priestly gifts of the foreleg, jaw and maw?
outcomeNote: The mishna lays down four rulings about exemption from the priestly gifts; no dispute, question or dialectic appears in this unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּכוֹר שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בְּמֵאָה, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמֵּאָה שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת כּוּלָּן – פּוֹטְרִים אֶת כּוּלָּן, אֶחָד שׁוֹחֵט אֶת כּוּלָּן – פּוֹטְרִים לוֹ אֶחָד.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to a blemished «firstborn» animal, which one may slaughter and eat without being required to give the foreleg, jaw, and maw to the priest, «that was intermingled with one hundred» non-sacred animals, from which one is required to give those gifts, in a case «when one hundred» different people «slaughter all of them,» each slaughtering one animal, one «exempts them all» from giving the gifts, as each could claim that the animal that he slaughtered was the firstborn. If «one» person «slaughtered them all,» one «exempts one» of the animals «for him.»

segments.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט לַכֹּהֵן וְלַגּוֹי – פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְהַמִּשְׁתַּתֵּף עִמָּהֶן – צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּרְשׁוֹם, וְאִם אָמַר: ״חוּץ מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת״ – פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת.
segments.en: «One who slaughters» the animal of a priest «for the priest or» the animal of a gentile «for the gentile is exempt from» the obligation to give «the gifts» of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw. «And» an Israelite «who enters into partnership with» a priest or a gentile «must mark» the animal to indicate that it is jointly owned and exempt from the obligation to give the gifts. «And if» a priest sold his animal to an Israelite and «said:» The animal is sold «except for the gifts» with it, the Israelite is «exempt from» the obligation to give «the gifts,» as they are not his.

segments.he: אָמַר: ״מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל פָּרָה״, וְהָיוּ בָּהֶן מַתָּנוֹת – נוֹתְנָן לַכֹּהֵן, וְאֵינוֹ מְנַכֶּה לוֹ מִן הַדָּמִים. לְקָחָן הֵימֶנּוּ בְּמִשְׁקָל – נוֹתְנָן לַכֹּהֵן, וּמְנַכֶּה לוֹ מִן הַדָּמִים.
segments.en: If the Israelite «said» to the one slaughtering the animal: «Sell me the innards of a cow, and there were gifts» included «with it,» i.e., the maw, the purchaser «gives them to the priest and he does not deduct» the value of the gifts «from the money» that he pays «him.» If «he bought» the innards «from» the slaughterer «by weight,» the purchaser «gives» the gifts, i.e., the maw, «to the priest and deducts» the value of the gifts «from the money» that he pays «him.»

moves.summary: a blemished firstborn intermingled with a hundred non-sacred animals exempts all of them when a hundred people slaughter, but only one when a single owner slaughters
slaughtering for a priest or a gentile exempts from the gifts; a partner must mark the animal; a sale 'except for the gifts' exempts the buyer
moves.about: a priest selling his animal to an Israelite stipulates that the priestly gifts in it are excluded from the sale, so the buyer owes the priest nothing for them

moves.cueHe: אמר: ״מכור לי בני מעיה של פרה״
moves.summary: buying innards outright, the purchaser gives the maw to the priest without deduction; buying by weight, he deducts its value from the price
moves.about: a buyer asks the butcher to sell him a cow's innards, which contain the maw that belongs to the priest
